_comment: A LAND AURA'S WILD MANA IS A BLUE SOURCE -- the user's own reference board, and the button
did not appear on it.
This is `references/EldraziDisplacerFlicker/claude_s1_gi0` at turn 3, reconstructed by
test/combo_off_sweep.py: Emiel, two Peregrine Drakes, two Clouds, an Aether Hub and a
Conservatory each carrying Trace of Abundance + Wild Growth, a Wild-Growth'd Mariposa, and a
LIVING WISH IN HAND. The turn the user WON. `offered=0`.
Rules 3, 4 and 5 (IN-HAND, WISH-DRAW, WISH-NODRAW) all require `UB` -- a blue or black source
-- and comborules::HasBlueOrBlackSource walked EffectiveProduces only. The board's only blue
is the two Trace of Abundance, whose 'one mana of any color' rides the host's tap
(cards.json: land_aura_produces []). Its sibling comborules::HasRedSource, twenty lines
above it in the same file, carried exactly the clause that counts them; the blue/black one
did not. One helper now answers both (MTG_COMBO_OFF_UB_AURA).
MEASURED, one card at a time, nothing else changed: as reconstructed offered=0; + Yavimaya
Coast offered=1; + Adarkar Wastes offered=1; + Kitchen offered=1 VERIFIED; + 2 energy (so the
Aether Hub's any-colour mode is live) offered=1 VERIFIED. After the fix the board as the user
actually had it is offered AND verified.
A land Aura's wild can never pay a {C} pip (ManaPool credits it as `wild`, deliberately not
`wild_c`), which is why the same clause must NOT be added to ColorlessSourceCount.
Reconstruction caveat, inherited from test/combo_off_frames.py: floating mana cannot be
staged, so this asks the frame with an EMPTY pool -- a strictly harder board than the one the
user sat in front of.
